title: Il futuro comincia domani
summary: Building the futuro semplice, its irregular stems, time markers, and the present-for-future

blocks.title: Il futuro semplice — build it from the infinitive
blocks.body: Drop the final **-e** of the infinitive and add one set of endings: **-ò, -ai, -à, -emo, -ete, -anno**. For **-are** verbs the stem vowel also flips *a → e*, so *parlare* becomes *parler-*: *parlerò*. Only *ò* and *à* carry a written accent — push the voice there.
blocks.callout: One set of endings for -are, -ere, and -ire alike — only the stem differs.

blocks.title: I verbi irregolari al futuro
blocks.body: A handful of high-frequency verbs shorten their stem before the same endings. Learn these five *io*-forms now — you'll use them constantly: **essere → sarò, avere → avrò, andare → andrò, fare → farò, venire → verrò**.
blocks.callout: sarò, avrò, andrò, farò — the four you can't avoid.

blocks.prompt: Complete: 'Domani io ___ con il capo.' (Tomorrow I'll talk with the boss.)
blocks.explain: *io* takes *-ò*: *parlerò*. The other two are *tu* and *lui/lei*.

blocks.title: Il presente per il futuro
blocks.body: For something near and already decided, Italian often just uses the **present tense** plus a time word: *Domani vado al mercato* (Tomorrow I'm going to the market). Save the futuro semplice for things that are further off, uncertain, or a promise.
blocks.callout: Near and settled → presente. Distant or unsure → futuro semplice.

blocks.title: Vicino e certo vs lontano e incerto

pairs.right: *Un giorno vivrò a Roma.* — futuro (lontano, incerto)
pairs.note: Use the present for near, settled plans. Save the futuro for distant, speculative, or promised things.

blocks.prompt: Say 'I will be home tomorrow' using essere in the futuro.
blocks.explain: *Sarò a casa domani.* Essere's futuro stem is irregular — sar- plus the same endings.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the whole line.

blocks.scene: At the bar, Marco asks about your plans for the weekend.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.en: So, what will you do this weekend?

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Sabato vado al mercato, e domenica forse andrò a correre.
lines.en: Saturday I'm going to the market, and Sunday maybe I'll go running.
lines.spotlight: Present for the near, decided plan (sabato); futuro for the more open one (forse... domenica).

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Io invece sarò impegnato venerdì sera — suonerò con la band.
lines.en: I'll be busy Friday evening — I'll play with the band.

lines.speaker: You
lines.en: Really? Where will the concert be?

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Sarà in un bar del centro.
lines.en: It'll be at a bar downtown.

lines.speaker: You
lines.spotlight: ci sarò — the futuro of esserci, 'to be there'.

blocks.prompt: Write three things you will do (or plan to do) in the next week — mix the futuro semplice with the present-for-future where it feels natural.
